text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
Female(x) ::: x is a female tennis player.
Male(x) ::: x is a male tennis player.
AtRolandGarros(x) ::: x is at Roland Garros 2022.
Question(x) ::: x is the question.
IgaS(x) ::: x is Iga Świątek.
RafaelN(x) ::: x is Rafael Nadal.
CocoG(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.
Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are one of the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaS) ∧ AtRolandGarros(x) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
∀x (Female(x) ∧ AtRolandGarros(x) → LostTo(x, IgaS)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtRolandGarros(x) → Female(x) ∨ Male(x)) ::: All tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (Male(x) ∧ AtRolandGarros(x) → LostTo(x, RafaelN)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros in 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
(RankedHighly(CocoG) ∨ LostTo(CocoG, RafaelN)) → ¬Male(CocoG) ∧ At
